title: At 20 plant transplant gradients, 39% of the cover gap from warm-site controls lay outside the spatial line
abstract: We tested whether a scalar fraction of progress could describe warmed plant community composition between origin and warm-site controls. We used independent TransPlant data. At the last common census, three to nine years after establishment, 39 cover contrasts in 20 gradients had mean progress of 0.525 along the spatial line. After a plot sampling-variance correction, 38.7% of the remaining squared cover gap lay outside that line (95% gradient bootstrap limits 28.2% to 50.0%). Plot occurrence gave 25.9% (16.5% to 42.0%) in 40 contrasts. Country weights, omission of two gradients with noted botanical issues, and removal of weak spatial contrasts gave similar results. An exploratory pool partition put 51.9% of the cover deviation in species found at both elevations. Thus incomplete progress on one spatial line cannot describe all of the gap. This does not reject species-specific lag models or establish a different equilibrium. Transplants change more than temperature, controls need not be a future state, and the correction assumes independent group mean errors. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Progress and departure from the spatial line in 20 plant transplant gradients. Limits use gradient resampling. The species-pool partition is exploratory.
